**Written Statement Regarding October 27 Afternoon Transportation**  
**Bus 41 | Route 9 | Fairmont Elementary**  
**To: Mrs. Okafor**  
**Copy: Darlene, Supervisor; Transportation Office**  
**From: [Driver’s Name]**  
**Date: [Date Submitted]**  
**Re: Complaint dated October 29 regarding Amara Okafor**

Dear Mrs. Okafor,

I am writing in response to your complaint dated October 29, which my supervisor, Darlene, provided to me on November 3. I want to explain what happened during the afternoon route on Tuesday, October 27, and why I returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary rather than letting her off at the stop at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. I understand that you were frightened when Amara did not get off the bus as expected. I am sorry for the worry and upset you experienced that afternoon.

My responsibility is to transport Amara safely and follow the district’s requirements for releasing kindergarten students. Amara has a green tag on her bag, indicating that an adult must be present at her stop. Under the district rule for kindergarten riders, if an adult is not present, the student must remain on the bus and be returned to school, where the office contacts the parent. That is the procedure I followed based on what I could see at the stop.

I arrived at Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street at 3:52 p.m. The scheduled arrival time is 3:50 p.m., so I acknowledge that I arrived two minutes after the scheduled time. I waited until approximately 3:55 p.m. During that time, I did not see an adult waiting at the corner to receive Amara. Because I could not confirm that an adult was there for her, I kept her on the bus.

At 3:56 p.m., I radioed dispatch to report the situation. Gloria at dispatch contacted the school. At that point, I still had three stops to complete and 14 children remaining on the bus. I completed the remaining stops and returned Amara to Fairmont Elementary at 4:31 p.m. I personally walked her into the school and handed her over to Mrs. Petrakis in the office.

I understand from the complaint that you were parked across Brandt Street near the laundromat and that you waved to me. I did not see you or your wave. There was a box truck parked on that side of the street. I cannot say for certain whether the truck blocked my view of you, but I can state that I did not see or recognize an adult there to receive Amara. I am not saying that you were not there. I am explaining what I was able to observe from the driver’s position when I had to make the decision about releasing her.

I also want to address your concern that I would not respond when you waved. I did not knowingly ignore you or refuse to acknowledge you. Had I seen your signal, I would have been aware that you were trying to get my attention. As it happened, I did not see it, and I proceeded according to the rule that applies when I cannot identify an adult waiting for a kindergarten student.

With children still aboard, I could not leave the bus unattended to go across the road and look for someone. I had to remain responsible for the students in my care while also making sure Amara was not released without an adult present to receive her. Keeping her aboard and notifying dispatch was the appropriate action available to me under the district’s procedure.

The complaint also states that I “drove off laughing.” I was not laughing. As we pulled away, I was directing a fourth-grade student in seat 2 to sit back down. I needed to address that student’s behavior while continuing to supervise the children and operate the bus safely. I want the written record to be clear about what I was doing at that time.

During the remainder of the trip, Amara appeared comfortable. She was coloring on her folder and asked whether she could ride more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip. My intention was to keep the explanation simple and reassuring for her. I offer these observations to describe how she appeared while in my care, not to minimize the concern you felt. I understand that her experience on the bus and your experience while waiting for her were very different.

I respectfully request that the Transportation Office promptly preserve and review the available camera footage from Bus 41 for the October 27 afternoon run, including our arrival at the stop, the waiting period, and our departure. I ask that any available audio from that period also be reviewed. The recording should be considered alongside this statement and your complaint so that the office can assess what it shows about the stop, my actions, and the exchange with the student in seat 2.

I have driven a school bus for 28 years without a write-up. I take that responsibility seriously, particularly when transporting young children who depend on adults to make safe decisions for them. I ask that this statement be included in the file with the complaint and that the record reflect that I followed the district’s procedure for a kindergarten student when I could not see an adult at the stop.

I am a grandparent, and I understand why not knowing where a child is would be frightening. I also hope you understand that my decision was made to protect Amara, not to disregard you. Going forward, I respectfully ask that you wait visibly on the bus side of the street, if that can be done safely and in accordance with the school’s stop instructions, or step out of your parked car where I can clearly see you. If there is uncertainty about where to wait, I would welcome the Transportation Office’s help in confirming a safe, visible pickup arrangement.

I am glad to continue driving Amara, and I want us to resolve this respectfully. My goal is for you to feel confident about her transportation and for me to be able to identify you clearly at the stop while following the safety requirements that apply to her.

Sincerely,

[Driver’s Name]  
Bus 41, Route 9
